edits.old: Speculative decoding changes both execution cost and the numerical history of a quantized runtime. When an application must reproduce a fixed ordinary greedy output, the designer needs to determine where to constrain execution and whether the qualified design pays. We study these decisions using natural donor-state crosses, a phase-scoped attention implementation, and paid ordinary and matched target-only baselines. CUDA and Vulkan crosses distinguish local current-path, retained-state and interaction effects. A separate B570 fork study finds unchanged immediate decisions but different trajectories under sustained alternate continuation. On RTX, a query-layout transformation retains batched projection and feed-forward work; target prefill and continuation form an inclusion-minimal passing set within a tested four-switch family. The frozen design qualifies full responses on 24 project-unused inputs. Generation speed is 1.170 times ordinary and 1.169 times matched target-only execution. Resident-request speed is 1.742 times ordinary but 1.035 times matched: the draft-free path change already gives 1.683 times. Seven tasks regress against matched request time, and one round reverses direction. Wider fixed-capacity drafting and a B570 endpoint repair qualify while losing performance. Separate M4 and 358H cases limit added control and draft-only optimization. The study connects implementation-specific diagnosis, finite qualification and paid comparisons to runtime choices, with repair evidence restricted to the tested Qwen3 family and configurations.
edits.new: Speculative decoding changes both execution cost and the numerical history of a quantized runtime. When an application must reproduce a fixed ordinary greedy output, the designer must identify where execution needs constraints and whether the qualified design reduces cost. We study these decisions with natural donor-state crosses, a phase-scoped attention implementation and paid ordinary and matched target-only baselines. CUDA and Vulkan crosses distinguish local current-path, retained-state and interaction effects. A separate B570 fork study finds unchanged immediate decisions but different trajectories under sustained alternate continuation. On RTX, a query-layout transformation retains batched projection and feed-forward work; target prefill and continuation form an inclusion-minimal passing set within a tested four-switch family. The frozen design qualifies full responses on 24 project-unused inputs. Generation speed is 1.170 times ordinary and 1.169 times matched target-only execution. Resident-request speed is 1.742 times ordinary but 1.035 times matched: the draft-free path change already gives 1.683 times. Seven tasks regress against matched request time, and one round reverses direction. Wider fixed-capacity drafting and a B570 endpoint repair qualify while losing performance. Separate M4 and 358H cases test the cost of added control and the limits of draft-only optimization. These results guide constraint placement and the choice to use speculation after qualification, with repair evidence restricted to the tested Qwen3 family and configurations.

edits.old: The other campaigns test three tempting shortcuts. First, global serialization can recover output while increasing cost. An earlier RTX arm qualifies 57/57 arrays on 19 exposed tasks but achieves $0.677\times$ target-only speed, with descriptive interval $[0.662,0.692]$ and no task faster. Its synchronized post-prefill-to-slot-release timer includes instrumentation and logging. It is a separate negative operating point, not an earlier point on the expansion's server-generation curve; Supplement \S S6.4 retains the host amendment and preceding V3 stop.

edits.old: Second, added control must pay for itself. The prospective M4 campaign has 60 tasks, three conditions, three repeats and 540 requests under a post-prefill contract. Always speculation and Guard each qualify 180/180 direct-ID comparisons. Target-only/Always speed is $1.347\times$, but the paired secondary Guard/Always latency ratio is 1.027, with descriptive interval $[1.013,1.044]$: the measured guard is slower. A hindsight oracle choosing only target-only or Always offers about 0.069\% further geometric-mean latency reduction. This narrow two-action opportunity does not bound intra-request policies; the primary and secondary statistical streams remain distinct (Supplement \S S6.6).

edits.old: Third, cheaper drafting may leave a target-work floor. On 358H, CPU/NPU drafting each qualifies 90 direct-ID comparisons but gives $0.734\times/0.352\times$ speed. With measured target work and committed progress fixed, eliminating every other nonnegative cost yields prompt-estimator ceilings of $0.837\times/0.845\times$. Even that idealization needs a uniform target-work reduction of at least 16.28\%/15.52\% to reach parity. Draft-only optimization cannot close this conditional budget; changing the target path or state interface requires new qualification and measurement. These are necessary budgets, not achieved optimizations or an impossibility result for NPUs (Supplement \S S6.7). M4 and 358H inform separate design decisions and do not replicate the RTX repair.

edits.old: Paid ordinary and matched comparisons then change the performance interpretation: $1.742\times$ RTX request speed includes a $1.683\times$ draft-free target-path gain, leaving $1.035\times$ from speculation on that path. The increment is uneven and reverses in one round. A wider qualified draft loses, B570 endpoint repair remains slower than strong baselines, and the separate M4/358H cases constrain the value of added control and draft-only optimization. These outcomes support a concrete design practice within the studied family: diagnose local dependence, qualify the complete output under an explicit configuration, then charge both baselines before selecting speculation.
